implementation_notes: Go's standard idiom puts the lookup service inside a package: a name-keyed table populated by Register functions from init() and an Open function that resolves the name to a registered implementation. database/sql shows the shape with sql.Register(name, driver), sql.Open(driverName, dsn) and sql.Drivers() for enumerating bindings, and the same structure appears in image, encoding and similar packages. The binding is process-global and written once during initialisation, so there is no cache to invalidate and no re-resolution - changing a binding means rebuilding the binary or loading a new module. What replaces the classic structure is the exported package-level registry plus the driver interface, so callers depend on the name and the interface and never on the implementation package.
pitfalls: sql.Register panics if the name is already taken or the driver is nil, so registration must happen exactly once (init), never from request paths or from tests that run twice.
sql.Open only validates the driver name and prepares the handle; the first real operation fails, so a successful lookup is not a reachable resource.
A registry with no removal is a permanent binding: anything that must come and go needs its own synchronised registry with an unregister path.

variants.name: Go plugin loading (plugin.Open + Lookup)
variants.implementation_notes: For genuinely dynamic resources Go offers plugin.Open(path), which loads a Go plugin shared object and returns a handle, and Plugin.Lookup(name), which resolves an exported symbol (variable or function) to a Symbol. The loader itself caches: opening a path that is already open returns the existing Plugin, so replacing a plugin means loading a new path and a fresh process - there is no unload. Platform support is limited (Linux, FreeBSD and macOS per the package documentation), which makes this realization unsuitable for portable applications.
pitfalls: Host binary and every plugin must be built with the same toolchain, build flags and dependency versions; a mismatch fails at load time or on the first call.
Plugins are currently supported only on Linux, FreeBSD and macOS (per the package documentation) and cannot be unloaded - each plugin pins its code for the process lifetime.
Plugin.Lookup returns a Symbol (any) that must be type-asserted; a wrong assertion panics, so validate the symbol type at the boundary.
